plant.bilberry.title: Bilberry
plant.bilberry.about_looks: A low bush that reaches a grown-up's knee, with small bright green leaves. Its berries are dark blue, and they turn your fingers and tongue blue.
plant.bilberry.about_grows: In shady spruce and pine forests, where it often covers the whole forest floor.
plant.bilberry.about_year: Small pink flowers in late spring. The berries are ripe from July to September. In autumn the leaves fall, and the green stems wait under the snow for spring.
plant.bilberry.about_fact: A bilberry is blue inside too, not only on the outside. Bears, foxes, birds and people all love to eat them.
plant.lingonberry.title: Lingonberry
plant.lingonberry.about_looks: A small bush with shiny, dark green leaves that stay green all winter. Its berries are bright red and taste sour.
plant.lingonberry.about_grows: In dry pine forests and on rocky hills, where the ground is sunny and sandy.
plant.lingonberry.about_year: Little white and pink bell-shaped flowers in early summer. The berries turn red in August and September, and some stay on the bush under the snow.
plant.lingonberry.about_fact: Lingonberries keep for a long time without going bad, so people have stored them for winter for hundreds of years.
plant.heather.title: Heather
plant.heather.about_looks: A low, woody bush with tiny leaves like scales. In late summer it is covered in small pink and purple flowers.
plant.heather.about_grows: On sunny rocks, dry heaths and at the edges of pine forests.
plant.heather.about_year: It flowers from July to September. The flowers dry on the stems and stay on, brown, all winter.
plant.heather.about_fact: Bees collect lots of nectar from heather in late summer. Heather honey is dark and has a strong taste.
plant.fly_agaric.title: Fly agaric
plant.fly_agaric.about_looks: A mushroom with a bright red cap covered in white spots. Its stem is white, with a white ring round it.
plant.fly_agaric.about_grows: In forests under birches, spruces and pines. It lives together with the trees' roots and helps them take food from the soil.
plant.fly_agaric.about_year: The red caps come up from August to October, and are gone after the first hard frosts.
plant.fly_agaric.about_safety: Very poisonous to people. Never eat it, and wash your hands if you have touched it. Look, but don't pick!
plant.fly_agaric.about_fact: Some animals, like red squirrels, can eat it without getting ill. People must never try.
plant.porcini.title: Porcini
plant.porcini.about_looks: A big, chubby mushroom with a brown cap like a bun. Under the cap there are no gills, only a soft sponge.
plant.porcini.about_grows: In spruce, pine and birch forests, often in the moss.
plant.porcini.about_year: It comes up from July to October, most of all after warm rain in late summer.
plant.porcini.about_safety: Some mushrooms are deadly poisonous and look like good ones. Only pick mushrooms with a grown-up who knows them well.
plant.porcini.about_fact: Red squirrels dry mushrooms for winter: they hang them on tree branches, like washing on a line.
plant.norway_spruce.title: Norway spruce
plant.norway_spruce.about_looks: A tall, dark green tree shaped like a cone, with short sharp needles. Its long brown cones hang down from the branches.
plant.norway_spruce.about_grows: In shady, damp forests. Under old spruces it is dim, and moss covers the ground.
plant.norway_spruce.about_year: The needles stay green all year. The cones ripen in autumn, and in late winter they open and drop their seeds onto the snow.
plant.norway_spruce.about_fact: Red squirrels pull spruce cones apart to eat the seeds. Look for chewed cone cores on the ground!
plant.scots_pine.title: Scots pine
plant.scots_pine.about_looks: A tall tree with an orange-brown trunk and a small green crown high at the top. Its long needles grow in pairs.
plant.scots_pine.about_grows: On dry, sunny ground: sandy heaths and rocky hills, where other trees find it hard to grow.
plant.scots_pine.about_year: The needles stay green all year. Its cones take two years to ripen.
plant.scots_pine.about_fact: A pine can live for hundreds of years. An old pine's thick bark protects it from forest fires.
plant.birch.title: Silver birch
plant.birch.about_looks: A tree with a white trunk and black patches. Its small leaves have edges like a saw.
plant.birch.about_grows: Almost everywhere: in forests, on meadows and by lakes. Birches are often the first trees to grow on open ground.
plant.birch.about_year: Light green leaves come out in May. In autumn they turn bright yellow and fall, and in winter the tree is bare.
plant.birch.about_fact: Moose eat birch leaves in summer and birch twigs in winter.
plant.rowan.title: Rowan
plant.rowan.about_looks: A small tree with leaves like feathers, each made of many small leaflets. In autumn it has bunches of bright red-orange berries.
plant.rowan.about_grows: At forest edges, in clearings and among other trees.
plant.rowan.about_year: White flowers in big clusters in early summer. The berries ripen in August, and the leaves turn red in autumn.
plant.rowan.about_fact: Rowan berries stay on the tree into winter, and flocks of birds, like waxwings and thrushes, come to eat them.
plant.aspen.title: Aspen
plant.aspen.about_looks: A tall tree with a smooth grey-green trunk and round leaves on long, flat stalks. The leaves shake and rustle in the slightest wind.
plant.aspen.about_grows: In forests, at forest edges and on rocky slopes. Aspens often grow in groups, all from the same roots.
plant.aspen.about_year: The leaves come out in May. In autumn they turn yellow, orange and red, and then fall.
plant.aspen.about_fact: Moose love aspen shoots and bark. Many animals live in old aspens, like woodpeckers and flying squirrels.
plant.wild_raspberry.title: Wild raspberry
plant.wild_raspberry.about_looks: A tall bush with small prickles, often taller than a child. Its leaves are green on top and white underneath. A ripe red berry comes off its stalk like a little hat, hollow inside.
plant.wild_raspberry.about_grows: In sunny clearings, along forest edges and paths, and where trees have been cut down.
plant.wild_raspberry.about_year: White flowers in June. The berries are ripe from late July into August. In autumn the leaves turn yellow and fall, and the brown canes stand in the snow all winter.
plant.wild_raspberry.about_fact: Each raspberry is made of many tiny round beads, and each bead has its own seed. A cane only gives berries in its second summer.
plant.crowberry.title: Crowberry
plant.crowberry.about_looks: A low green mat that hugs the ground, with tiny leaves like short needles. Its berries are shiny and black.
plant.crowberry.about_grows: On rocky hilltops and dry heaths, often next to heather and lingonberry, and in bogs.
plant.crowberry.about_year: Tiny purple flowers in April and May, hard to spot. The black berries are ripe from late July, and many stay on the plant under the snow until spring.
plant.crowberry.about_fact: When the snow melts in spring, last year's crowberries are still there: a welcome meal for hungry birds and foxes.
plant.red_clover.title: Red clover
plant.red_clover.about_looks: A meadow flower with round, pinkish-red flower heads. Each leaf has three leaflets, often with a pale V on them.
plant.red_clover.about_grows: In meadows, on roadsides and around old farms, where it is sunny. Not inside the dark forest.
plant.red_clover.about_year: Its leaves come up in late spring. It flowers from June to September, and dies back in the winter.
plant.red_clover.about_fact: Each flower head is made of many tiny flowers. Only bumblebees have tongues long enough to reach the sweet nectar inside.
plant.white_clover.title: White clover
plant.white_clover.about_looks: A small clover that creeps along the ground, with round white flower heads. Its leaves have three round leaflets.
plant.white_clover.about_grows: On lawns, paths, roadsides and meadows, wherever the grass is short.
plant.white_clover.about_year: It flowers from June to September. The leaves stay green until the snow comes.
plant.white_clover.about_fact: Sometimes a leaf has four leaflets instead of three. People say finding one brings good luck!
plant.goat_willow.title: Goat willow
plant.goat_willow.about_looks: A big bush or small tree with grey-green stems and broad oval leaves, grey and soft underneath. In spring it is covered in fluffy catkins.
plant.goat_willow.about_grows: On forest edges, in clearings and on the shores of lakes.
plant.goat_willow.about_year: The catkins open in April, before the leaves: silvery and soft at first, then bright yellow. The leaves turn yellow in October and fall.
plant.goat_willow.about_fact: Its catkins are the first food of the year for bumblebee queens waking up in spring. In winter, hares and moose nibble its twigs.
plant.wavy_hair_grass.title: Wavy hair-grass
plant.wavy_hair_grass.about_looks: A grass with leaves as thin as hair, growing in soft tufts. Its flower heads are airy and wavy, and shine silver and purple.
plant.wavy_hair_grass.about_grows: On dry forest floors, in clearings and on rocky slopes. It is the commonest grass in Finnish forests.
plant.wavy_hair_grass.about_year: It flowers in June and July, and the stalks turn the colour of straw by autumn. The leaves stay green under the snow.
plant.wavy_hair_grass.about_fact: Hares and voles graze it all year round, even digging for it under the snow in winter.
plant.chanterelle.title: Chanterelle
plant.chanterelle.about_looks: An egg-yellow mushroom shaped like a little funnel or trumpet. Under the cap it has soft ridges instead of gills.
plant.chanterelle.about_grows: In mossy spruce and mixed forests, often in small groups.
plant.chanterelle.about_year: It comes up from July to early October, most of all in August.
plant.chanterelle.about_safety: Some mushrooms are deadly poisonous and look like good ones. Only pick mushrooms with a grown-up who knows them well.
plant.chanterelle.about_fact: Chanterelles smell a little like apricots. They are a favourite of Finnish mushroom pickers, and of slugs too.
plant.fireweed.title: Fireweed
plant.fireweed.about_looks: A tall plant, often taller than a child, with long narrow leaves and a spike of bright pink flowers on top.
plant.fireweed.about_grows: In big patches on clearings, roadsides and forest edges, and on burnt ground.
plant.fireweed.about_year: It flowers in July and August, from the bottom of the spike up. In autumn its leaves turn red and its pods let out white fluffy seeds.
plant.fireweed.about_fact: It is called fireweed because it is one of the first plants to grow back after a forest fire. Its fluffy seeds can fly far on the wind.
plant.wood_anemone.title: Wood anemone
plant.wood_anemone.about_looks: A small spring flower with one white flower, often a little pink underneath, above three deeply cut leaves.
plant.wood_anemone.about_grows: In leafy groves and herb-rich spruce forests, where it can cover the ground like snow.
plant.wood_anemone.about_year: It flowers in late April and May, before the trees get their leaves. By midsummer its leaves have withered, and it waits underground until next spring.
plant.wood_anemone.about_safety: Poisonous if eaten. Look, but don't pick.
plant.wood_anemone.about_fact: Ants carry its seeds away to eat a tasty bit on them, and so they plant new wood anemones.
plant.reindeer_lichen.title: Reindeer lichen
plant.reindeer_lichen.about_looks: Pale grey-green cushions made of many fine branches, like tiny antlers. It is crisp when dry and soft after rain.
plant.reindeer_lichen.about_grows: On dry, rocky hilltops in pine forests, and on sandy heaths.
plant.reindeer_lichen.about_year: It looks the same all year. It grows very slowly, only a few millimetres a year.
plant.reindeer_lichen.about_fact: A lichen is a fungus and a tiny green alga living together as one. In Lapland, reindeer dig it out from under the snow to eat in winter.
plant.red_stemmed_feathermoss.title: Red-stemmed feathermoss
plant.red_stemmed_feathermoss.about_look: A soft moss with feathery, yellow-green shoots on red stems. It grows in thick, springy carpets.
plant.red_stemmed_feathermoss.about_grow: Almost everywhere on the floor of spruce and pine forests, together with bilberry and lingonberry.
plant.red_stemmed_feathermoss.about_year: It stays green all year, and in winter it sleeps under the snow.
plant.red_stemmed_feathermoss.about_fact: Squirrels and birds pull it up to line their nests: it makes a soft, warm bed.
plant.juniper.title: Juniper
plant.juniper.about_looks: A prickly evergreen bush, often tall and narrow like a column, with sharp grey-green needles. Some bushes have round berries, green and blue-black.
plant.juniper.about_grows: On dry rocky heaths, sunny slopes and old pastures.
plant.juniper.about_year: It is green all year. Its berries take two years to ripen, so green and blue ones hang on the bush together.
plant.juniper.about_fact: Junipers can live for hundreds of years. Thrushes eat the berries and spread the seeds.
plant.bracken.title: Bracken
plant.bracken.about_looks: A big fern with one tall stalk and a wide, flat, triangle-shaped leaf held out sideways, up to a metre high.
plant.bracken.about_grows: In patches in spruce and mixed forests and on forest edges.
plant.bracken.about_year: In late May its new leaves come up curled like a fist, then unroll. After the autumn frosts they turn rusty brown and lie down under the snow.
plant.bracken.about_safety: Poisonous to eat. Look, but don't pick.
plant.bracken.about_fact: Ferns have no flowers or seeds. They spread with spores: brown dust as fine as smoke, made under their leaves.
plant.spiny_wood_fern.title: Spiny wood fern
plant.spiny_wood_fern.about_looks: A fern with a loose ring of light green leaves, finely cut like lace, rising from one spot and bending outwards.
plant.spiny_wood_fern.about_grows: In damp spruce forests and on shady, mossy ground.
plant.spiny_wood_fern.about_year: New leaves unroll in May. In late autumn most of them turn yellow-brown and wither under the snow.
plant.spiny_wood_fern.about_fact: Under its leaves you can find little brown dots in late summer. They are full of spores, the fern's tiny seeds.
plant.lily_of_the_valley.title: Lily of the valley
plant.lily_of_the_valley.about_looks: Two broad, upright green leaves and a stalk of small, white, sweet-smelling bells. Later it has round red berries.
plant.lily_of_the_valley.about_grows: In patches in dry leafy groves, on forest edges and on rocky slopes.
plant.lily_of_the_valley.about_year: The white bells flower in June. The red berries are there in August and September.
plant.lily_of_the_valley.about_safety: Every part of it is very poisonous, the red berries too. Never eat it, and wash your hands if you have picked it. Keep pets away from it.
plant.lily_of_the_valley.about_fact: It is the national flower of Finland.
plant.staghorn_coral.title: Staghorn coral
plant.staghorn_coral.about_looks: Light brown branches with pale tips, like the antlers of a stag. A bush can be 2 metres wide.
plant.staghorn_coral.about_grows: In warm, clear, shallow sea water on reefs in the Caribbean Sea.
plant.staghorn_coral.about_year: It looks the same all year. Once a year, a few nights after the August full moon, it lets tiny eggs drift up into the sea.
plant.staghorn_coral.about_fact: A coral is not a plant: it is made of thousands of tiny animals. Little fish hide between its branches.
plant.brain_coral.title: Grooved brain coral
plant.brain_coral.about_looks: A round, yellow-brown dome with deep winding grooves, like a big brain. It can be 2 metres wide.
plant.brain_coral.about_grows: On reefs in the warm Caribbean Sea, from shallow water down to about 40 metres.
plant.brain_coral.about_year: It looks the same all year. It grows very slowly, only a few millimetres a year.
plant.brain_coral.about_fact: A big brain coral can be hundreds of years old. It is made of many tiny animals living side by side.
plant.sea_fan.title: Common sea fan
plant.sea_fan.about_looks: A flat purple fan of fine branches on a short stalk, up to almost 2 metres tall.
plant.sea_fan.about_grows: On reefs in the warm Caribbean Sea, where the water moves.
plant.sea_fan.about_year: It looks the same all year. It sways back and forth with the waves.
plant.sea_fan.about_fact: A sea fan stands across the current, like a net, so its tiny animals can catch food from the water.
plant.red_mangrove.title: Red mangrove
plant.red_mangrove.about_looks: A tree on tall arching roots, like stilts, with thick shiny green leaves.
plant.red_mangrove.about_grows: In salty shallow water along warm coasts of America and West Africa, where the tide comes and goes.
plant.red_mangrove.about_year: Its leaves stay green all year. Its long green seedlings start growing on the tree, then drop into the water.
plant.red_mangrove.about_fact: Its stilt roots make a safe place for baby fish, crabs and young sharks.
plant.baobab.title: African baobab
plant.baobab.about_looks: A huge tree with a very thick grey trunk and short branches that look like roots in the sky.
plant.baobab.about_grows: In dry, hot savannas in Africa.
plant.baobab.about_year: It drops its leaves in the dry season and is bare for months. Big white flowers open at night, then furry fruits grow.
plant.baobab.about_fact: Its trunk stores water like a barrel. Some baobabs are more than a thousand years old.
plant.coconut_palm.title: Coconut palm
plant.coconut_palm.about_looks: A tall, thin, bending trunk with long feathery leaves at the top and coconuts under them.
plant.coconut_palm.about_grows: On sandy beaches by warm tropical seas all around the world.
plant.coconut_palm.about_year: It is green all year and has coconuts at every time of year.
plant.coconut_palm.about_fact: A coconut can float across the sea for weeks and grow into a new palm on another beach.
plant.italian_cypress.title: Italian cypress
plant.italian_cypress.about_looks: A tall, narrow, dark green tree shaped like a candle flame.
plant.italian_cypress.about_grows: On dry, sunny hills around the Mediterranean Sea.
plant.italian_cypress.about_year: It is green all year. Its small round cones turn from green to grey-brown.
plant.italian_cypress.about_fact: Its wood smells nice and lasts a very long time. Some cypresses are over a thousand years old.
plant.umbrella_thorn.title: Umbrella thorn acacia
plant.umbrella_thorn.about_looks: A tree with a wide, flat crown like an umbrella, small feathery leaves and long white thorns.
plant.umbrella_thorn.about_grows: On dry savannas and in deserts in Africa and the Middle East.
plant.umbrella_thorn.about_year: It keeps some leaves all year. Small round white flowers come before the rains, then curly seed pods.
plant.umbrella_thorn.about_fact: Giraffes eat its leaves with their long tongues, right between the sharp thorns.
